title: Victoria counts votes as Coalition eyes end of 12 years of Labor rule
excerpt: Counting is under way in Victoria, with the Coalition tipped to win and One Nation leading early in four regional seats on tiny counts.
content_html:
Votes are being counted across Victoria after polls closed at 6pm on Saturday, with the Coalition under Jess Wilson widely tipped to end 12 years of Labor government and One Nation chasing its first lower house seats in the state.

Counting is at a very early stage. At 6.37pm AEDT, less than 1 per cent of the vote had been counted and no seat had been won. The Victorian Electoral Commission has said it will not declare any official results tonight.

Early figures

In the first small batches of votes, One Nation led in four regional seats held by the Nationals: Gippsland East, Lowan, Mildura and Morwell. Each had less than 1 per cent of its vote counted.

In Gippsland East, which the Nationals hold by about 25 per cent, One Nation had about 55 per cent of the primary vote from a single booth of 38 votes. Early figures from a handful of booths can change sharply as larger centres report.

The Liberals were ahead in South-West Coast and Caulfield, the Nationals in Shepparton, Labor in Oakleigh and Mill Park, and the Greens in Pascoe Vale.

The contest

Labor went into the election notionally holding 56 of the 88 lower house seats, the Coalition 29 and the Greens three. A party needs 45 seats to govern in its own right.

Premier Ben Carroll, who replaced Jacinta Allan as Labor leader in July, campaigned for a fourth term while weighed down by the state's debt. Polls before election day suggested he could also be at risk in his own seat of Niddrie.

Wilson, who became Liberal leader in November last year, spent the final days of the campaign defending plans for privatisation and cuts to kindergarten funding that the Coalition revealed late.

Final polls had the Coalition ahead but differed sharply on One Nation, which led by Warren Pickering in Victoria polled anywhere from 16 to 25 per cent. Analysts have said the party needs to lead the primary vote in a seat to win it. Greens leader Ellen Sandell described the election as a four-way contest.

More than half of Victoria's eligible voters cast their ballots before election day, and voters in parts of the state contended with severe weather on Saturday.

What comes next

Results are expected to firm through the evening as pre-poll and larger booths report, though close seats may take days to settle. In the 40-seat upper house, a YouGov projection before polling day suggested One Nation could win about 11 seats and hold the balance of power.

This story will be updated as the count progresses.
